gallery.title: File:20180603 Maastricht Heiligdomsvaart 225.jpg
gallery.description: View of a historic religious procession during the 2018 Heiligdomsvaart ("Relics Pilgrimage") in Maastricht, Netherlands. The history of this seven-yearly catholic pilgrimage goes back to the Middle Ages. The first 'modern' version took place in 1874. On both Sundays of the 10-day festival, a procession is held in which the main relics of the town and other devotional objects are exhibited. This photo was taken from the spectator stand in Vrijthof square at the end of the (second) procession on 3 June 2018. The marching band that closes the procession is Harmonie Sint Petrus en Paulus from the Maastricht neighbourhood and parish of Wolder.

gallery.title: File:Beer Coaster Design - Flickr - brewbooks.jpg
gallery.description:
I was thinking about how networks of processors work - while sitting having a beer in Maastricht. These notes are circa 1991.
At the time, I was working with Transputer based systems.  The transputer was  a microprocessor architecture of the 1980s, featuring integrated memory and serial communication links, intended for parallel computing. It was designed and produced by Inmos. We programmed these in occam  a concurrent programming language.

gallery.description: Evening view of Grote Staat at the corner of Vrijthof in Maastricht, the Netherlands. The blue and gold banners refer to the 2018 "Heiligdomsvaart" (Pilgrimage of the Relics). The history of the seven-yearly Heiligdomsvaart goes back to the Middle Ages. The first 'modern' version of this ten-day catholic pilgrimage took place in 1874. The 2018 Heiligdomsvaart was the 55th edition.
